did_you_know.text: Zechariah sees four horns in a vision. According to the angel’s interpretation, the horns represent the powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.
Opposite the four horns are four craftsmen—skilled workers—who were sent to deal with them.
The four craftsmen’s task is to terrify the horns and overthrow the power of the nations that raised a horn against the land of Judah and scattered its inhabitants.
A man carrying a measuring line sets out to measure Jerusalem, but the vision emphasizes that the city will be too large to be enclosed by a wall.
Jerusalem is described as an unwalled city—open and without a surrounding wall—because of the great number of people and animals within it.
The Lord promises to be a wall of fire around Jerusalem and to be its glory within—a divine protection and presence in the city.
Those living in the land of the north and in Babylon are called to leave their places of exile and return to Zion.
The passage emphasizes how sensitive the Lord is to harm done to his people through the image: “Whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye.”
The vision also includes many nations: they will join themselves to the Lord and become his people, while the Lord will dwell among them in Zion.
The chapter ends with a call for all humanity to be silent before the Lord, because he has already risen from his holy dwelling.
